title: Mara and the Songbook
premise: Kestrel Coldharbour has spent ten years answering anonymous letters left in her bookshop's returned-books bin, falling in love with a voice she never expected to meet. When Wren Ashby — the letter writer, her childhood friend presumed lost at sea, and the person whose survival cost Kestrel her family's reputation — moves in next door, the truth of that night finally surfaces. As Wren's health fails from the injury sustained saving Kestrel's life, Kestrel must forgive herself for surviving before she can claim the love waiting in those pages. The book ends with Wren recovering through winter and the two of them writing one last letter together: an invitation to their own wedding, tucked into the songbook where it all began.
about_author: Odile Winterbourne is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's daughter who grew up on coastal romances and salt-stained paperbacks. She writes love stories about people who mistake endurance for solitude.

chapters.title: The Returned-Books Bin
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She closes the shop on a rainy Tuesday and finds a new letter in the bin — the first in months — asking whether forgiveness can be posted like mail. We learn of her daughter Ivy, her late husband, and the decade-long correspondence with 'W.' Emotional beat: longing disguised as routine.

chapters.title: A Moving Van Next Door
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A quiet stranger with a cane and a familiar handwriting sample moves into the cottage beside the shop. Kestrel recognizes the slant of the letters but convinces herself she's imagining it. Emotional beat: dread braided with hope.

chapters.title: What the Sea Kept
chapters.summary: Wren's POV flashback to the storm ten years ago: the capsized boat, the choice to pull Kestrel from the water instead of Kestrel's brother, and the injury that ended a singing career. Wren wrote letters as penance. Emotional beat: guilt wearing devotion's face.

chapters.title: Tea, Tentatively
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Kestrel invites the neighbor for tea; conversation circles without landing. Wren quotes a line only 'W.' ever wrote, and Kestrel goes cold mid-pour. Neither names what they both know. Emotional beat: the almost-recognition that changes everything.

chapters.title: The Songbook
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds the old songbook — half ballads, half unsent confessions — in Kestrel's attic while helping after a shelf collapse. Reading it, Wren realizes Kestrel loved the letters back, and that the truth will wound more than silence. Emotional beat: terror of being fully known.

chapters.title: Ivy Asks Questions
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Ivy befriends the neighbor and innocently reveals that Mama still reads 'the bin letters' aloud on bad nights. Kestrel confronts Wren; the identity is confirmed, then shattered by the revelation about her brother. Emotional beat: betrayal arriving hand-in-hand with relief.

chapters.title: Winter Takes the Shop
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A blizzard forces the shop closed; Wren collapses from the old injury and Kestrel, despite everything, keeps them alive through the night. In the fever hours, Wren confesses everything — including that the brother's death was not Wren's fault, a fact Kestrel has never let herself examine. Emotional beat: forced intimacy stripping defenses.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Climax approaches: Kestrel rereads every letter chronologically and sees, for the first time, that her anger at Wren was armor against her own survivor's guilt. She visits her brother's memorial and speaks the truth aloud. Emotional beat: the beginning of self-forgiveness.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Letters
chapters.summary: Climax. Kestrel lays all 120 letters across the shop floor and asks Wren to read them together, start to finish, no omissions. Grief, laughter, and fury pass between them until only love remains. Wren's health crisis peaks and passes; Kestrel chooses to stay. Emotional beat: catharsis and commitment.

chapters.title: An Invitation, Tucked Inside
chapters.summary: Resolution, spring. The shop reopens with a new bin labeled 'Letters Answered.' Wren teaches Ivy the recovered songs; Kestrel writes the final letter — a wedding invitation — and slips it into the songbook for a stranger to find. Emotional beat: belonging earned, survival made worth its price.
